note: Facts and sources behind the member descriptions in MS.json, gathered 2026-10-05. "review" holds research notes for a human check; "issues" lists open questions.

byways.name: Beach Boulevard Scenic Byway
byways.where: Beach Boulevard (former Old Highway 1), Cedar Point in Bay St. Louis to Bayou Cadet, Waveland; Hancock County

facts.fact: Beach Boulevard, formerly Old Highway 1, follows the Hancock County coast about 13 miles from Cedar Point in Bay St. Louis, across US 90, through Bay St. Louis and Waveland to the fishing village of Bayou Cadet.
Sights along it include Buccaneer State Park, the former Customs House and a Pirate's House said to be linked to Jean Lafitte.

byways.name: Brice's Crossroads Battlefield-Chief Tishomingo Scenic Byway
byways.where: Grisham St in Baldwyn, MS 370, CR 833, CR 503 and MS 348 to MS 145 at Guntown; Lee County

facts.fact: The route starts at the Brice's Crossroads interpretive center in Baldwyn (milepost 0) and follows Grisham Street, MS 370, CR 833, CR 503 and MS 348 to its end at MS 145, milepost 12.8; the last half mile is in Guntown.

Granite markers along MS 370 describe the battle of June 10, 1864 between Forrest and Sturgis, and a new footbridge stands where the wartime bridge crossed Tishomingo Creek, named for the Chickasaw chief Tishomingo.
The interpretive center at 607 Grisham Street is now called Mississippi's Final Stands Interpretive Center.

byways.review: CMP gives 12.8 miles and the MDOT map 12.4; catalog line is 15.4 miles, worth checking its ends.

byways.name: Byways to Space Scenic Byway
byways.where: Six routes in the Stennis Space Center buffer zone, Hancock County: MS 607, US 90 toward Pearlington, MS 604, Logtown Road, Old Highway 43 (Napoleon), Texas Flat Road

facts.fact: Byways to Space is a network of six routes covering more than 30 miles in or near the 125,000-acre buffer zone of NASA's Stennis Space Center, often under oaks.

The routes are named for communities closed when the buffer zone was created, among them Logtown, Napoleon, Westonia and Santa Rosa; the NASA Scenic Byway to Space segment is the four-lane MS 607 to the center's gates.
Stennis Space Center is described as the nation's largest rocket engine test facility.

byways.review: Catalog entry is named for one segment (NASA Scenic Byway to Space, MS 607); its 37-mile line and bbox appear to cover the whole six-route network, so it is matched to the network.

byways.name: Delta Bluffs Scenic Byway
byways.where: DeSoto County: Austin Rd and Delta Bluff Rd from MS 301 to Walls; MS 301 from Austin Rd to Arkabutla Lake; Old MS 304 from I-55 at Hernando to Bluff Rd

facts.fact: The byway has three branches: Delta Bluff Road west from MS 301 to the Great River Road at Walls, MS 301 from Austin Road to Arkabutla Lake, and Old MS 304 from I-55 west to Bluff Road.
On the northern branch the road crosses rolling farmland and then drops into the Mississippi River delta, showing the change from hills to delta.
The byway runs through Hernando's four historic districts and out into DeSoto County farmland.

byways.review: Not in catalog; no agency GIS line found.

byways.name: Grand Gulf-Raymond Scenic Byway
byways.where: Back Grand Gulf Rd, Ingleside-Karnac Ferry Rd, Willows Rd and Old Port Gibson Rd, Grand Gulf Military Monument to Raymond; Claiborne and Hinds counties

facts.fact: The route runs from Grand Gulf Military Monument on the Mississippi along Back Grand Gulf Road, Ingleside-Karnac Ferry Road, Willows Road and the Old Port Gibson Road to the Raymond Military Park, about 50 miles.
The first ten miles wind through loess bluffs in deep fern-lined cuts under live oaks and bald cypress hung with Spanish moss, then the road follows high ground about forty miles to Raymond.
In 1863 a journalist with Grant's army called it a well-traveled thoroughfare; the old dirt road is now paved.

byways.name: Great River Road
byways.where: US 61 and MS 1 along the Mississippi River, Helena Bridge to the Louisiana line (joins the Mississippi Delta Great River Road and the Lower Mississippi Historic Byway)

facts.fact: MDOT describes the Great River Road National Scenic Byway as running more than 275 miles along the Mississippi following US 61, joining the Lower Mississippi Historic Byway and the Mississippi Delta Great River Road.
In Mississippi the road passes the antebellum homes of Natchez, the Delta Blues Museum in Clarksdale and the Vicksburg battlefield, through farmland planted in soybeans, rice and cotton.

byways.review: Catalog road is the ten-state Great River Road; MDOT's National Scenic Byway section is the sum of the two state byways below.

byways.name: Gulf Coast Scenic Byway
byways.where: US 90 along the beachfront from the Bay St. Louis bridge through Pass Christian, Long Beach and Gulfport to about MS 605; Harrison County

facts.fact: The Gulf Coast Scenic Byway is an 18-mile stretch through Pass Christian, Long Beach and Gulfport, and parts of it are in National Register multiple resource districts.
Many historic buildings in the three downtowns and along the beachfront were destroyed by Hurricane Katrina in 2005.
MDOT's map draws the byway along US 90 on the beachfront, 19 miles, ending near MS 605.

byways.review: Not in catalog; MDOT text says 18 miles and its map 19 miles. Route identified from MDOT map (US 90).

byways.name: Gateway to History
byways.where: MS 463 from Reunion Pkwy to MS 22; MS 22 west to Petrified Forest Rd near Flora and east to Canton; MS 16 and MS 43 from Canton to the Natchez Trace; Madison County

facts.fact: The byway has four segments totaling 32.8 miles: MS 463 north from Reunion Parkway to MS 22, MS 22 west to the Petrified Forest near Flora, MS 22 east to Canton, and MS 16 and MS 43 from Canton to the Natchez Trace.
Madison County created the Mannsdale-Livingston preservation district along MS 463 in 2005, and Livingston, the county's first seat in 1824, is being recreated as Livingston Township.
Governor Phil Bryant signed the bill designating the byway in March 2013.

byways.review: Not in catalog; not labeled on MDOT's 2018 statewide PDF map. No agency GIS line found.

byways.name: Highway 605 Scenic Byway
byways.where: MS 605 from US 90 north across I-10 to MS 67, Gulfport-Biloxi area; Harrison County

facts.fact: MDOT's map shows the Highway 605 Scenic Byway as 15 miles of MS 605 from US 90 north to MS 67.
MS 605 is an expressway; before 2004 the part between I-10 and US 90 was MS 975 and the part north of I-10 was MS 981.
Mississippi Power's Plant Jack Watson stands on MS 605.

byways.review: Not in catalog. MS 605 continues north of MS 67 to Saucier; MDOT map ends the byway at MS 67. No corridor plan or description found on MDOT's page.

byways.name: Highway 67 Scenic Byway
byways.where: MS 67 from US 49 near Saucier to MS 15 and I-10 at D'Iberville; Harrison County

facts.fact: MS 67, a four-lane highway completed in 2007, runs 20.68 miles from US 49 to MS 15 and on to I-10, through Saucier, Tradition and Woolmarket, and bisects the De Soto National Forest.
The Biloxi potter George Ohr collected his clay from the MS 67 corridor.
MS 67 ends at an interchange with US 49 at the north end of Saucier.

byways.review: Not in catalog; no agency GIS line found.

byways.name: Lower Mississippi Historic Scenic Byway
byways.where: US 61 from the Issaquena-Warren line through Vicksburg, Port Gibson, Natchez and Woodville to the Louisiana line, with spurs on Grand Gulf Rd, Rodney Rd/MS 552 and US 84

facts.fact: The byway follows US 61 from Warren County through Claiborne, Jefferson and Adams counties to the Louisiana line in Wilkinson County, more than 100 miles, linking Vicksburg, Port Gibson, Natchez and Woodville.
Side routes go to Grand Gulf Military Park and west on Rodney Road past the Shaifer House and the Ruins of Windsor, returning past Alcorn State University on MS 552.
Clark Creek's waterfalls lie west of Woodville on MS 24, and the road passes St. Catherine Creek Wildlife Refuge south of Natchez.

byways.name: Mississippi Delta Great River Road Scenic Byway
byways.where: US 49 at the Helena Bridge, MS 1 to Onward, US 61 to the Issaquena-Warren line; Coahoma, Bolivar, Washington, Sharkey and Issaquena counties

facts.fact: The byway runs about 175 miles from the Helena Bridge to the Issaquena-Warren county line, through Coahoma, Bolivar, Washington, Sharkey and Issaquena counties.
It enters the state on US 49 at the Helena Bridge, follows MS 1 to US 61 at Onward, then US 61 south toward Vicksburg; a commercial stretch in Greenville is segmented out.
The Mississippi River levee forms a backdrop along much of the route, past fields that go white with cotton in early fall.

byways.review: Catalog line is 218 miles with a bbox reaching 34.99 N (the Tennessee line); the state byway starts at the Helena Bridge (about 34.3 N). Catalog line may include US 61 through Tunica and DeSoto counties, which is not part of this byway.

byways.name: Natchez Trace Parkway
byways.where: Natchez Trace Parkway, Natchez northeast through Jackson and Tupelo to the Alabama line

facts.fact: The parkway is a 444-mile road through three states that roughly follows the Old Natchez Trace, used by American Indians, Kaintucks, settlers and soldiers.
About 312 of its miles are in Mississippi, starting at Natchez.
MDOT's program guidelines name the Natchez Trace Parkway as the state's All-American Road.

byways.review: Managed by the National Park Service; MDOT lists it among Mississippi's byways.

byways.name: Noxubee Hills Route
byways.where: Choctaw Lake (Choctaw County) through the Tombigbee National Forest and past Bluff Lake to US 45; Choctaw, Oktibbeha, Winston and Noxubee counties

facts.fact: The route stretches from Choctaw Lake through the Tombigbee National Forest past Bluff Lake in the Noxubee refuge to US 45, through Choctaw, Oktibbeha, Winston and Noxubee counties.
It is 43 miles long, of which 14.5 miles are unpaved.
Along it are reminders of mills once powered by artesian wells and the first Lutheran church in Mississippi.

byways.review: Not in catalog; no agency GIS line found.

byways.name: William Faulkner Scenic Byway
byways.where: MS 30 from CR 14 at New Albany (Union County) to CR 229 near Oxford (Lafayette County)

facts.fact: The byway is a 15.7-mile stretch of MS 30 between CR 14 near New Albany and CR 229 near Oxford, almost entirely in the Holly Springs National Forest.
Points along it include Puskus Lake, the Little Tallahatchie River and Greenfield Farm, Faulkner's mule farm near the Union-Lafayette county line.
In 2014 the Legislature named MS 30 between New Albany and the county line the William Faulkner Memorial Highway.

byways.review: Not in catalog; MDOT text says 15 miles, CMP and map 15.7. No agency GIS line found.

issues: MDOT program page is a JavaScript app; the list was read in a browser. It lists 14 entries (Highway 605 and 67 under one heading). The 2014 guidelines name nine state byways plus the Great River Road and Natchez Trace; Gulf Coast and William Faulkner (CMP dated 2014) are newer, and the guidelines do not list the Delta and Lower Mississippi river byways separately.
MDOT's 2018 statewide PDF map does not label Gateway to History, though the program page and its own map PDF include it.
On the MDOT page the Byways to Space section repeats a paragraph from Delta Bluffs about Hernando (copy error on the agency page).

Catalog mississippi-delta-great-river-road-64069 (218 mi) extends to about 34.99 N; the state byway begins at the Helena Bridge on US 49 and runs MS 1 and US 61 south (~175 mi). Check whether the catalog line includes US 61 through Tunica and DeSoto counties.

Catalog lower-mississippi-historic-scenic-byway-62295 carries a National Scenic Byway flag; MDOT treats the Great River Road as the national byway, made of the two state river byways. Not a contradiction but worth a look.
Catalog nasa-scenic-byway-to-space-81465 is named for one of six segments (MS 607); its line appears to cover the network. Consider renaming to Byways to Space Scenic Byway.
Brice's Crossroads catalog line is 15.4 mi vs 12.8 mi in the CMP and 12.4 mi on MDOT's map.
Highway 605 Scenic Byway has no corridor plan or description on MDOT's page; extent (US 90 to MS 67, 15 mi) is read from MDOT's map only.
Several corridor plans (Byways to Space, Grand Gulf-Raymond, Hwy 67, Noxubee, Faulkner, Lower Mississippi, Delta GRR) are scanned PDFs; facts from them were taken by OCR.
Catalog lists Natchez Trace Parkway also as a National Forest Scenic Byway; not checked here.
